events.title: King Charles I Is Beheaded
events.description: Charles I of England was executed outside the Banqueting House in Whitehall, London. He had been convicted of treason by a High Court of Justice set up by Parliament.
events.significance: The public execution of a reigning monarch was a radical break with tradition. It ushered in the English Commonwealth and shaped later debates about the limits of royal power.

events.title: First Assassination Attempt on a U.S. President
events.description: At the U.S. Capitol, Richard Lawrence aimed two pistols at President Andrew Jackson. Both misfired. Jackson, enraged, reportedly went after the attacker with his cane before bystanders subdued the man.
events.significance: It was the first attempt on the life of a sitting American president. It also raised lasting questions about presidential security.

events.title: Hitler Becomes Chancellor of Germany
events.description: President Paul von Hindenburg appointed Adolf Hitler Chancellor of Germany. The move followed political maneuvering among conservative leaders who believed they could control him.
events.significance: The appointment began the Nazi regime's rapid consolidation of power. It set the stage for World War II and the Holocaust.

events.title: Mahatma Gandhi Is Assassinated
events.description: Gandhi was shot and killed in New Delhi while walking to an evening prayer meeting. He was 78, and his death came only months after India won independence.
events.significance: The loss of the leading figure of nonviolent resistance stunned the world. It also left a lasting mark on India's early years as a nation.

events.title: Bloody Sunday in Derry
events.description: British soldiers opened fire on civil rights demonstrators in Derry, Northern Ireland, killing 14 people.
events.significance: The killings deepened the Troubles and boosted support for paramilitary groups. They remained a source of public anger and calls for justice for decades.
